conventions: A universal relative that the ASV fuses into one -soever word is headed on the relative wherever one stands in the unit: bekol 'asher (1.7, 1.9) and 'el kol 'asher (1.16) -> *whithersoever* take 'asher as source head, with kol, which carries the -soever, named as the competing reading in each note under rule 8. Where no relative stands in the unit the quantifier heads it instead, as kol 'ish -> *Whosoever he be* does at 1.18. All four are `aligned` fusions under rule 30 rather than `noncompositional`, since each has a defensible internal head; the corpus records both statuses for kol 'asher -> *whatsoever* and neither is wrong.

The correlative *so* answering a ka'asher clause is not read as one connective's correlative pair. Rule 14's *both ... and* sentence governs a connective morpheme rendered by a pair, and a comparative *as ... so* is not that. Where ken stands in the apodosis it takes the *so* (1.17); where none stands the *so* is its own `added` unit (1.5), which is what rule 14's own added-connective sentence directs for an apodosis connective no morpheme answers to. One chapter writes both shapes.

An *even* standing before an appositional phrase is placed by which morpheme is present. At 1.4 a waw stands before 'ad, so the bare *even* is the connective's and only *unto* is the preposition's (rule 16's first limit). At 1.2 neither a connective nor an object marker stands, and the appositive's own le- takes the whole *even to*, on the reasoning by which rule 16 gives a fronting le- the *as for* of a topicalized phrase. The competing reading, marking that *even* `added` under rule 16's appositional limit, is named in the unit's note.
report: Checked all 37 candidate lemma groups, and read the dump end to end for the split the table cannot see, since it is keyed by source lemma and so blind to the chapter's two `added` units. Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by what the ASV writes or by a difference in the source morphemes. No patches.

Preposition le- (31 occurrences, the largest group): the R->Vqc difference is le'mor under rule 27 (1.1, 1.10, 1.11, 1.12, 1.13, 1.16) against purpose and complement infinitives where the ASV writes *to* (1.6, 1.7 twice, 1.8, 1.11 three times). The R->Sp2mp/Sp3mp difference tracks the English exactly: *to you* (1.3) and *to them* (1.2) are written, while *give them*, *giveth them*, *giveth you*, *gave you* (1.14, 1.15), *Prepare you* and *have given your brethren rest* are bare indirect objects, so the preposition is unrepresented under rule 40. Each of the nine bare cases was checked against its own clause.

Article ha- (39 occurrences): every unrepresented article stands in a phrase whose one written determiner is a demonstrative (this Jordan 1.2/1.11, this Lebanon 1.4, this people 1.2/1.6, this land 1.13, This book 1.8) or is an agreement article beside a word already holding the phrase's *the* (rule 47). Every aligned one has a *the* standing before its own word. Rule 29's count was run phrase by phrase and comes out both ways inside the chapter: two *the*s written and nothing fronted at 1.4 (the land of the Hittites, the going down of the sun), 1.10 and 1.11; one *the* written and fronted from an anarthrously rendered rectum at 1.12 (the half tribe of Manasseh) and 1.14 (the mighty men of valor). That is what rule 29 turns on, not a split.

Object marker 'et (17): unrepresented wherever the ASV writes the object bare, including both 1.13 markers; the *against* and *unto* of 1.18 are rule 16's first family (rebel against, hearken unto), and the 1.10 marker is bare because *commanded the officers* spends no word on the object relation. ka'asher fuses to one *as* at 1.3, 1.5 and 1.17b, and is split *According*/*as* at 1.17a because the ASV writes two words there and kol stands between the morphemes; the b-plus-construct pairs fuse where one rendering is written (*beyond* 1.14/1.15, *before* 1.5/1.14, *within* 1.11) and split where the ASV writes a word for each (*through the midst* 1.11). Rule 30's one-rendering condition accounts for all of them.

The *even* pair is the closest call in the chapter and is licensed by the source: 1.4 has a waw before 'ad, so the bare *even* is the connective's and *unto* the preposition's, exactly as rule 16's first limit directs; 1.2 has no connective and no marker, so the appositive's own le- takes *even to*. Rule 16 decides the two oppositely and both notes name the competing reading, so this is a difference the source licenses rather than a split. I did not disturb either edge.

The -soever fusions are consistent: bekol 'asher and 'el kol 'asher -> *whithersoever* (1.7, 1.9, 1.16) all head on the relative, with kol named as the competitor in each note. 1.18's kol 'ish -> *Whosoever he be* heads on kol, but no relative stands in that unit, so it is a different morpheme set and not the same construction analysed twice. Recorded as a convention.

The two `added` units are the only supplied English not folded into a licensing morpheme, and each has a counterpart in the chapter where a morpheme does license the same word: 1.5's correlative *so* is added because no ken stands, while 1.17 writes ken and it takes the *so*; 1.15's *he hath given* is added under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause, with nothing parallel elsewhere. No verse folds such a word into a neighbouring rendering, so the shape the table cannot see is clean too.

BSB: all 27 disagreements are documented convention differences and none is a genuine error. 14 le- are rule 27's le'mor and rule 40's bare indirect objects; 10 ha- are demonstrative-determined phrases and agreement articles under rules 41 and 47; JOS.1.3's Sp3ms is the relative clause's resumptive suffix, left unrepresented under rule 22 because the ASV writes *that ... upon* rather than *whereon*; the two JOS.1.13 markers are rule 16 object markers on a bare object. BSB attaches each of these to its host phrase, which is its stated convention.

The three large-source-unit candidates (1.7 unit 29, 1.9 unit 18, 1.16 unit 13) are the *whithersoever* fusions and are indivisible under rule 30: one English word carries the direction, the relation and the universal. Size alone flagged them.
